assays.assay_name: Open Field Test (locomotor activity / ethanol-induced behavioral sensitization)
assays.assay_description: Circular wooden arena (40 cm diameter, 50 cm high, open top, floor divided into 19 squares); locomotion frequency (square entries) hand-scored by a blind observer in 10-min sessions. Used for basal activity, ayahuasca-induced spontaneous locomotion, acute ethanol hyperlocomotion, sensitization development (Exp 1, day 10), ethanol sensitization phase, 8-day ayahuasca counter-sensitization, and saline/ethanol challenges (Exp 2).

application_type.evidence: All solutions were given intraperitoneally (i.p.) at a volume of 10 ml/kg of body weight.

setup_habituation.evidence: Eighty mice were given a 10-min habituation period in the open field on 2 consecutive days after a saline i.p. injection.

setup_restrain.evidence: animals were individually exposed to the open field arena for 10-min sessions (free-moving arena, no restraint mentioned)

food_restriction.evidence: Food and water were available ad libitum throughout the experiments (home cage); no food in the open-field arena during testing.

water_restriction.evidence: Food and water were available ad libitum throughout the experiments (home cage); no water in the open-field arena during testing.

time_to_assay.evidence: initial exposure to the open field environment 30 min after treatment; ethanol challenge 40+5 min after ayahuasca; sensitization test 7 days later; Exp 2: 30 min after each daily ayahuasca dose, saline challenge 4 days and ethanol challenge 6 days after last ayahuasca

sample_size.evidence: Six groups of animals were formed (n = 10 or 30) [Exp 1, 80 mice]; Six groups of animals were formed (n = 11 for each group) [Exp 2, 66 mice]

outcomes.summary: Ayahuasca (30–500 mg/kg) did not alter spontaneous locomotion, but at 300 and 500 mg/kg blocked acute ethanol-induced hyperlocomotion and at all doses prevented development of ethanol-induced behavioral sensitization. Eight days of ayahuasca (100 or 300 mg/kg) did not induce sensitization per se, and counter-sensitization blocked reinstatement of ethanol sensitization on ethanol challenge.
outcomes.statistics: Spontaneous: F(5,74)=0.41, p=0.83; acute ethanol: F(6,73)=11.74, p<0.0001 (Tukey p<0.05 for Aya300/500 vs Sal-Eth); sensitization: F(7,72)=7.87, p<0.0001 (Tukey p<0.05 all Aya vs Sal-Eth-Eth); counter-sensitization phase: pretreatment F(1,60)=0.370, p=0.54, treatment F(1,60)=0.282, p=0.75, time F(1,60)=1.57, p=0.21; saline challenge: F(1,60)=2.43, p=0.12; ethanol challenge interaction F(2,60)=4.95, p<0.01
outcomes.evidence: at the doses of 300 and 500 mg/kg, ayahuasca prevented the acute stimulating effect of ethanol... Treatment with ayahuasca at all doses before the first ethanol administration prevented the development of ethanol-induced sensitization... counter-sensitization with ayahuasca at both doses was effective in blocking the expression of the reinstatement of ethanol-induced behavioral sensitization.

judge_notes: Merged deepseek4's six OFT entries (spontaneous, acute ethanol, sensitization, counter-sensitization, saline challenge, ethanol challenge) into one Open Field assay: same apparatus, same measure, different drug conditions/timepoints/experiments.
B1 scored 0 (one measure: locomotion frequency); gemma's score 1 with value '1' and deepseek's '2-3' were inconsistent with the paper.
B6 kept at 0 (modal); locomotor sensitization is a drug-response measure, not a learning task.

D3 overridden to 2-7: qwen summed days across separate cohorts and gemma's own 13-day list does not reach 15+; only days 19 and 26 of counter-sensitization had reported data, giving 7 reported days in Exp 2.
DOI set to null: all three candidates gave different DOIs and the masthead lacks one.

Ethanol added as a separate dosing entry (1.8 g/kg = 1800 mg/kg; the Drugs section's '1.8 mg/kg' is a typo). Ayahuasca schedule set to chronic because of the 8-day daily regimen in Exp 2; Exp 1 was acute.
Age set to adult (3-month-old), following the modal candidate value.
